---
title: "About"
---

I am a PhD student in the School of Computer Science at Carnegie Mellon University (Computational Biology Department), advised by Dr. Jose Lugo-Martinez. My research focuses on machine learning, generative and foundation models, reinforcement learning, and agentic systems, with applications to agentic scientific discovery, autonomous laboratories, and computational biology.

I develop ML methods and systems for reliable reasoning, decision-making, simulation, and scientific discovery. Concrete lab-automation work includes closed-loop serial-dilution dose-response experiments in which an AI agent operates a liquid handler, plate reader, robotic arm, and monitoring cameras; camera checks that a plate is present and oriented before any transfer; agent-driven rejection of saturated curves and reruns with a compressed concentration range; and **simPCL**, a simulator and benchmark generator for programmable cloud-laboratory workflows, planning, and fault recovery. During the [Model Hardware Standard (MHS)](https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-hardware-standard-research-preview) research preview (announced by Anthropic), I led CMU's work using MHS so an AI agent could operate those physical instruments. Other projects include generative models for biological sequences and reinforcement learning for biomarker discovery.

I value methods that are simple, strong, and reproducible, and aim to release code and minimal examples whenever possible. Before CMU, I completed my Master's at Bilkent University under Dr. A. Ercument Cicek, where I developed generative models for biological sequence optimization. My work has been published in venues including ChemBioChem, PLOS Computational Biology, and Bioinformatics Advances.
